articles.title: Gcore Makes Enterprise Security Bundle Free for Public Agencies Until End of the Year
articles.summary:
Contern, Luxembourg, October 22nd, 2026, CyberNewswire Gcore is offering its WAAP Enterprise plan free of charge to any government body or public agency until December 31, 2026. The offer follows the php2shell vulnerabilities that forced public websites offline across Europe earlier this week. Gcore WAAP blocks the php2shell attack path (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) by default […]

The post Gcore Makes Enterprise Security Bundle Free for Public Agencies Until End of the Year appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Major U.S. Banks Detect Unauthorized AI Agents Operating Inside Customer Accounts
articles.summary:
Major U.S. banks are detecting third-party AI agents inside customer accounts, raising concerns that automated tools could act beyond the instructions customers give them. Some agents have contacted call centers or appeared to attempt independent actions, according to an Axios report published October 22, citing people familiar with the matter. articles.title: eMudhra Exits Global SSL/TLS Certificate Business Following the Vulnerability Disclosure
articles.summary:
eMudhra Limited has announced it is exiting the global SSL/TLS certificate business after disclosing weak private keys in eight intermediate certificate authority certificates. The October 22, 2026, decision follows emergency browser protections and growing questions about the company’s certificate issuance controls. eMudhra said its other digital trust services remain unaffected. In its official announcement, the company said […]

The post eMudhra Exits Global SSL/TLS Certificate Business Following the Vulnerability Disclosure appeared first on Cyber Security News.

articles.title: Claude Security Now Scans Repositories Continuously to Find Flaws and Track Fixes
articles.summary:
Anthropic has updated Claude Security so it can keep checking connected code repositories as they change, rather than waiting for a person to start each scan. The service also tracks reported vulnerabilities after developers make changes, marks them fixed when a correction is detected, and reopens them if they return. The updated product is in […]

articles.title: A New Extortion Gang Is Naming Companies on the Dark Web and Counting Down to Data Leaks
articles.summary:

The operation puts public pressure on organizations before their breach claims have been independently verified. The group began appearing in threat monitoring records around September 2026 and […]

articles.title: Hackers Were Targeting Critical PHP Vulnerabilities Days Before They Were Patched
articles.summary:
A threat actor tried to exploit two critical PHP vulnerabilities four days before the flaws were publicly disclosed and patched, according to Amazon Threat Intelligence. The activity began on October 17, 2026, while the vulnerabilities were still under coordinated disclosure. The flaws, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and known together as PHP2Shell, can allow remote […]

articles.title: Hackers Planted Malware on Japanese Cloud Servers, Forcing the Provider to Shut Down Its Service
articles.summary:
Hackers planted malware in customer server environments at Japan’s Onamae.com Desktop Cloud, prompting the provider to begin shutting down servers across every service plan. The company listed 26,739 servers as potentially affected, raising concerns about stored data and login details. That figure describes the possible scope, not a confirmed count of infected systems. The provider […]

articles.title: North Korean Hackers Use Post-Quantum Encryption to Hide New Malware From Security Tools
articles.summary:
North Korean-linked Lazarus hackers are using post-quantum cryptography in a malware delivery chain designed to conceal later-stage payloads from security tools. The technique appeared in Operation FlashHole, a campaign targeting organizations in South Korea. Instead of relying on encryption alone to hide files on disk, the malware uses a modern key-establishment method to protect payloads […]

articles.title: A Hacker Tried to Turn an AI Chatbot Into a Tool for Attacking Other Servers
articles.summary:
An exposed artificial intelligence platform can give an intruder more than a place to send messages. If it connects to stored credentials, company data, or network tools, the platform may also provide a route toward those resources. articles.summary:
